implemented_capabilities.capability: Eligibility-gap analysis (unmet requirements for a competition)
implemented_capabilities.notes: Parameterized Cypher over (Person)-[:HAS]->(Resource {status})-[:SATISFIES]->(Requirement)<-[:REQUIRES]-(Competition). A requirement is a gap when no ready Resource satisfies it. recommendNext runs two queries (coverage + decision status) and merges/sorts in JS by fewest missing then soonest ISO deadline because the author reports FalkorDB dropping a follow-up OPTIONAL MATCH after an aggregating WITH.

Writes (Person)-[:DECIDED]->(Decision {status joined|abandoned|submitted|candidate, at ISO string, note})-[:ABOUT]->(Competition) with bound params; recommendNext filters out abandoned/submitted contests. Append-only, no supersession or revocation.

implemented_capabilities.capability: Keyword intent router with optional LLM polish
implemented_capabilities.notes: Regex routing to six tools and a hard-coded alias table mapping phrases to competition ids; an optional MiniMax call rewrites the tool JSON (truncated to 3500 chars) and falls back to deterministic templates. No LLM tool-calling.

implemented_capabilities.capability: Read-only demo twin when FalkorDB is unavailable
implemented_capabilities.notes: On connect failure (and always on Vercel) answers come from a hard-coded JavaScript copy of the seed data; remember_decision returns a read-only message. The mode flag is returned so callers can tell, but the same answers appear without a graph.

graph_models_and_cypher: FalkorDB graph 'CompGraph'. Labels: Person{id:'self'}, Competition{id,name,url,deadline ISO string,mode,fee,prize_note,host}, Requirement{id,kind,detail}, Resource{id,kind,status ready|missing|blocked}, Decision{id,status,at,note}. Edges: HAS, SATISFIES, REQUIRES, DECIDED, ABOUT (COULD_ENTER, SAME_HOST, SIMILAR_TO mentioned in schema comments). Plain openCypher (OPTIONAL MATCH, collect, list comprehension, CASE). Dates stored as ISO strings because the author notes no datetime(). No APOC/GDS or algo procedures; no indexes defined.
algorithms: Requirement coverage set difference (all_reqs minus covered_kinds) and rank by (missing_count, deadline) in JS (tools.js:recommendNext)
backend_interfaces: Express: GET /api/health, GET /api/competitions, POST /api/ask {question, tool, competitionId, status, note, limit}, static UI and SPA fallback
Scripts: npm run load (scripts/load.sh, load.mjs) seeds the graph from cypher/seed-synthetic.cypher
frontend_interfaces: Vanilla JS page (web/index.html, app.js, styles.css) rendering an SVG path/gaps/recommendation visualization from graphPath payloads
agent_or_memory_mechanisms: Single-user decision memory in the graph (Decision nodes written by remember_decision and read back to filter recommendations). No multi-agent or state-machine logic.
security_findings: server/index.js:~27 - app.use(cors()) allows any origin; no authentication on POST /api/ask which can write Decision nodes in live mode

scripts/load.mjs:~24-36 - execSync builds a docker exec ... redis-cli GRAPH.DELETE shell command from FALKORDB_CONTAINER and GRAPH_NAME env vars (shell injection if env is attacker-controlled; also hard-deletes the graph on every load); dev script only
server/llm.js:~27-45 - sends tool result JSON to an external LLM endpoint (MiniMax) with a bearer key from env when set; failures degrade silently to the template
server/tools.js:~143 - note sanitization replaces ';' with ',' (unneeded because the value is a bound parameter; suggests the author considered statement splitting)
cypher/seed-synthetic.cypher (head) - seed data contains the owner's personal name, a Devpost handle and personal-status notes; not secrets but personal data in a public repo
No eval/exec/pickle; no hard-coded API keys found
duplicates_or_overlaps: Eligibility/requirement-satisfaction gap analysis is a generic 'what is missing before X is allowed' pattern; no direct duplicate in this batch. Decision memory overlaps Agent Memory & Provenance repos but is much thinner.
evidence_drift_relevance: LOW - a timestamped Decision node linked ABOUT a subject and a Resource.status that gates eligibility are minimal decision lineage and dependency-satisfaction signals; no provenance sources, supersession or validity windows.

strongest_reusable_unit.why: The unmet-REQUIRES Cypher (OPTIONAL MATCH ready satisfier, collect, size()=0) is a concise requirement-coverage check that could be ported to Python for 'dependency not satisfied' gating; everything else is demo scaffolding.
strongest_reusable_unit.external_runtime_needed: FalkorDB; Node runtime (code is JavaScript, would need a Python port)

strategy_rationale: A small single-user Node demo with a personal domain, a hard-coded demo twin and no tests; only the requirement-coverage Cypher idiom is worth borrowing, and it would need a Python rewrite.
